chunks: He said: "I will never send him with you until you give me a pledge from God that you will bring him back to me, unless you are surrounded (by misfortune)." When they had given him their pledge, he said: "God is witness to what we say."

key_terms.يُحَاطَ: to be surrounded or overtaken (by misfortune)

ai.seo_question: What condition did Prophet Jacob set before sending Joseph with his brothers?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Jacob (Ya'qub) insists on a divine pledge (mawthiqan min Allah) rather than a mere human promise, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the reliability of the patriarchs and the gravity of their covenants. The phrase 'unless surrounded' (illa an yuhatta bikum) is interpreted by exegetes as a concession to external force or death, highlighting Jacob's prudent yet trusting nature. This moment underscores the theme of divine protection amidst familial trials, a central motif in the Surah Yusuf.
